selection_rule: Every statement by an in-scope officeholder quoted in a story published on Nov. 14 or 15, 2026 in the NPR Politics and PBS NewsHour Politics feeds, as read on Nov. 15. PBS NewsHour carries Associated Press reporting. Two NPR audio segments with no transcript were skipped. Quotes under five words were left out, and two entries that were a commentator's account of what an official said were removed. No original source (transcript, release or post) could be read for any statement, so all wording is as the outlet reported it.
lede: Fifty-six statements by 15 officeholders appeared in two days of NPR and PBS NewsHour politics coverage. Most were about three things: the Nov. 13 nationwide ground stop and what it will cost to fix air traffic control, the Iran war and talk of ending it, and what Democrats plan to do with the majorities they won on Nov. 3.

Eleven of the 56 were checked. Eight were factual claims. Three were opinions or predictions resting on a factual premise, and for those the premise alone was rated. Five came out supported, including the transportation secretary's statement that air traffic control has seen decades of underinvestment. One was contradicted: the transportation secretary's reported account of what caused the ground stop differs from the FAA's own published account, though the FAA says its investigation is still open. Four were unsettled, meaning evidence was found but does not decide them: the president's statement that much of the air traffic control system is 50 years old, the Florida governor's statement about what a state law requires, a congressman's statement that his party won in places it had never won, and the premise behind the secretary of state's statement about economic pressure on Iran. One was unsupported, meaning no evidence was found for it; that is not a finding that it is false.

Three statements are linked to a direct counter-statement: two to a statement by another official on this page, and one to the FAA's own published account. A link shows that the two disagree on the same point. It is not a finding about which is right.
The other 45 are opinions, predictions, promises and one personal attack. They are listed because they were said, not because they can be checked, and are folded under each speaker.

statements.finding: AskAmerica's Medicaid enrollment data shows 75.8 million people enrolled in Medicaid and CHIP in January 2026, 39.7 million of them adults, which bounds the figure. evidence.label: health.medicaid_chip_enrollment_monthly (January 2026)
evidence.sql:
SELECT reporting_period,
       SUM(total_medicaid_chip_enrollment) AS total,
       SUM(adult_medicaid_enrollment) AS adults,
       SUM(child_enrollment) AS kids
FROM health.medicaid_chip_enrollment_monthly
WHERE report_status = 'U' AND reporting_period = '202601'
GROUP BY reporting_period

KFF, The Medical Frailty Exemption from Medicaid Work Requirements

statements.finding: AskAmerica's Senate returns for 1976-2024 show Texas last elected a Democratic senator in 1988, and 2026 coverage reports a Democratic win there, along with Kansas (reported as the first Democratic senator since 1932) and South Carolina (first in nearly 30 years). The 2026 results are from news reports, not certified returns.

evidence.label: officials.senate_race_results (U.S. Senate returns, 1976-2024)
evidence.sql:
SELECT state_name, MAX(cycle_year) AS last_d_win, COUNT(*) n
FROM officials.senate_race_results
WHERE state_name IN ('Texas','Kansas','TEXAS','KANSAS')
  AND leader_party_major = 'D' AND is_decisive
GROUP BY state_name

statements.speaker: Jason Crow

source.note: No original transcript or post located.

statements.finding: AskAmerica's returns for 1976-2024 show a Democratic U.S. House win in all 50 states and a Democratic U.S. Senate win in 47. Of the three states with none (Idaho, Kansas, Utah), Democrats won only Kansas in 2026. Coverage reports their last Kansas Senate win was in 1932; that predates the record and was not read from a primary source. House districts and state legislative seats were not tested.

evidence.label: officials.senate_race_results (U.S. Senate returns, 1976-2024)
evidence.sql:
SELECT state_postal,
       sum(case when leader_party_major='D' then 1 else 0 end) d_wins,
       max(case when leader_party_major='D' then year end) last_d,
       sum(case when leader_party_major='OTHER' then 1 else 0 end) oth,
       max(case when leader_party_major='OTHER' then year end) last_oth,
       sum(case when leader_party_major is null then 1 else 0 end) nullp
FROM officials.senate_race_results
WHERE is_decisive
GROUP BY state_postal
ORDER BY d_wins, state_postal

evidence.label: officials.house_race_results (U.S. House returns, 1976-2024)
evidence.sql:
SELECT count(distinct state_postal) states,
       count(distinct state_postal) FILTER (WHERE leader_party_major='D') dem_states
FROM officials.house_race_results
WHERE is_decisive
